rows.grounds: Compound expressing reason: limited seers cannot conceive the deity; ablative sense of cause.

items.question: Why can limited seers not conceptually grasp the deity?
premises: Limited seers possess restricted vision.
The deity exceeds their conceptual capacity.
What exceeds conceptual capacity is unimaginable to them.
items.inference: Therefore the deity is unimaginable by limited seers.
items.plain_english: This is because those with limited vision cannot conceive of the deity.

rows.grounds: Object of worship.
Instrumental indicating the means or formula used in worship.
Prescriptive injunction for ritual worship.

items.question: By what means should the deity be thoroughly worshipped?
premises: The deity is the object of worship.
A specific means is prescribed for worship.
The avarga serves as that prescribed means.
items.inference: Therefore one should thoroughly worship the deity with the avarga.
uncertainties: The precise technical referent of avarga in this ritual context is not specified here.
items.plain_english: One should thoroughly worship the god using the avarga.

rows.grounds: Predicate attributing worship-worthiness.

items.question: What status of worship-worthiness is affirmed for the deity?
premises: The deity is presented as an object of reverence.
Reverence entails worship-worthiness.
Worship-worthiness is explicitly affirmed.
items.inference: Therefore the deity is worthy of worship.
uncertainties: The implied subject is not explicitly stated in this token.

rows.grounds: Concessive compound with sandhi-marked fusion indicating 'even if having form'.
Negation particle.
Indefinite adjective qualifying impossibility.
Subject asserting absence of logical or doctrinal difficulty.

items.question: Does possessing form create any impossibility for the deity?
premises: The deity may be considered as having form.
Having form could be thought to entail impossibility.
No such impossibility is admitted.
items.inference: Therefore even in having form there is no impossibility.
items.plain_english: Even if the deity has form, there is no impossibility in that.

rows.grounds: Connective particle linking to prior discussion.
Compound naming a graded or sequential method.
Long compound indicating applicability to arrangements in subsequent chapters.
Quotation or concluding marker.

items.question: What purpose does sequential practice serve in later chapters?
premises: Sequential practice is introduced as a method.
Later chapters involve arrangements or placements.
This method is useful for those later arrangements.
items.inference: Therefore sequential practice is useful for the arrangements in the second and later chapters.
items.plain_english: And thus, sequential practice is useful for the arrangements that will occur in the second and later chapters.

rows.grounds: Present passive participle indicating what is to be contemplated as pervaded.
Prescriptive injunction for contemplative awareness.

items.question: How should the pervaded reality be contemplatively apprehended?
premises: A reality is presented as being pervaded.
Contemplation is prescribed as a practice.
The pervaded reality is the object of that contemplation.
items.inference: Therefore one should contemplatively apprehend what is being pervaded.
uncertainties: The specific referent of what is pervaded is not stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate that which is being pervaded.

rows.grounds: Relative pronoun indicating the subject whose condition changes.
Contrastive particle.
Instrumental indicating the sole means causing dissolution of limitation.
State of limited individuality to be dissolved.
Verb describing the dissolution of limitation.
Concluding marker.

items.question: What effect does mere ritual placement have on atomic limitation?
premises: A practitioner undergoes ritual placement.
Mere placement can be efficacious.
Atomic limitation is subject to dissolution.
items.inference: Therefore by mere placement the practitioner's atomic limitation dissolves.
items.plain_english: But for whom atomic limitation dissolves by mere placement alone, thus it is said.

rows.grounds: Compound naming the barrier of consciousness-form to be pierced.
Absolutive indicating prior action.
Emphatic particle.
Past participle describing what has come forth.
Prescriptive injunction for visualization.
Prescriptive injunction for meditative cultivation.

items.question: How should emergence through the wall of consciousness be visualized?
premises: There is a wall of consciousness-form.
This wall can be pierced.
Emergence follows piercing and should be imagined and meditated upon.
items.inference: Therefore one should imagine and meditate on what has emerged after piercing the wall of consciousness-form.
items.plain_english: Having pierced the wall of consciousness-form, one should imagine and meditate on what has emerged.

rows.grounds: Genitive indicating those for whom the rite is performed.
Locative compound specifying the ritual occasion.
Instrumental agent performing the application.
Present passive participle describing the procedure in use.
Concluding marker.
Indicates the remaining part of the procedure.

items.question: Who applies the remaining procedure during the disciples' initiation?
premises: An initiation time for disciples is specified.
A procedure is being applied at that time.
The teacher is the agent of application.
items.inference: Therefore the remainder is what is being applied by the teacher at the disciples' initiation time.
items.plain_english: Thus, the remainder is what is being applied by the teacher at the time of the disciples' initiation.

rows.grounds: Demonstrative pronoun referring to previously mentioned elements.
Connective particle.
Instrumental indicating the mode or method of application.
Gerundive expressing obligation or prescription.
Compound specifying the spatial range of application.

items.question: How and where should these elements be ritually applied?
premises: Certain elements are to be applied.
A specific manner of application is prescribed.
The application extends from head to feet.
items.inference: Therefore these elements should be applied in the Brahma manner from head to feet.
uncertainties: The exact technical meaning of brahmabhaṅgyā is not fully specified here.
items.plain_english: And these should be applied in the Brahma manner, from the head down to the feet.

rows.grounds: Compound describing a form whose parts are not yet differentiated.
Object to be imagined in meditation or ritual.
Gerundive prescribing visualization.

items.question: In what condition should the divine form be imagined?
premises: The divine form is an object of imagination.
A form can be imagined with or without differentiated parts.
The prescribed condition lacks differentiated parts.
items.inference: Therefore the divine form should be imagined with unmanifest limbs.
items.plain_english: The divine form should be imagined with its limbs not yet differentiated.

rows.grounds: Dative compound expressing the purpose of the ritual act.
Compound naming the ritual placement of kalās.
Gerundive prescribing the action.
Concluding marker.
Compound indicating the summary sense of the teaching.

items.question: What is the condensed purpose of performing the placement of kalās?
premises: The placement of kalās is prescribed.
Ritual acts serve a demonstrative purpose.
The stated purpose is to show the pervasion of Īśāna.
items.inference: Therefore the condensed meaning is that the placement of kalās is to be done to show the pervasion of Īśāna.
items.plain_english: The condensed meaning is this: the placement of the kalās should be performed to show the pervasion of Īśāna.
